title: polyjose conformance vector
description: One file under conformance/vectors/ holds exactly one vector. Every platform runner (Rust, WASM, Node, Kotlin, Swift) must reject a file that does not match this schema, and must fail (never skip) a vector whose operation it does not implement. Operations without an input/expect definition here are reserved for the features that will define them; until then no runner implements them, so a vector using one fails. Bytes under test of the codec operations (b64url.*, jwk.thumbprint) are given in lowercase hex, never base64url, so the codec is not checked against itself. The jws.* operations give octets as canonical base64url (members ending in _b64u), the form JWS fields natively have; the codec is not under test there. The keys.* operations give keys as PEM text, JWK objects and DER as canonical base64url (der_b64u), never hex.

source.description: Where the expected value comes from: an RFC section ("RFC 7638 §3.1"), an upstream suite, or "polyjose" for a project-defined negative vector.

description.description: What the vector checks, in one sentence.

hex.description: Lowercase hexadecimal, two digits per octet; empty for zero octets.

base64url.description: Characters of the base64url alphabet (RFC 4648 §5), no padding.

count.description: A non-negative integer that an unsigned 32-bit integer holds (ADR 0030 u32), so every binding reads it natively and exactly.

jws.description: A JWS: a string in the Compact Serialization (RFC 7515 §7.1), or an object in the flattened or general JWS JSON Serialization (RFC 7515 §7.2), which a runner passes to the library as its JSON text. Otherwise unconstrained: malformed JWSs are under test.

alg_list.description: An algorithm allow-list (RFC 8725 §3.1) of JWS "alg" names, passed to the library as given. An empty list, "none" or an unknown name is refused by the library with AlgorithmNotAllowed, which vectors may test.

failure.description: The operation must fail with exactly this error code.

b64url_encode_input.description: Octets to encode as unpadded base64url (RFC 7515 §2).

b64url_encode_ok.description: Encoding cannot fail, so only a success expectation exists.

b64url_decode_input.description: Text to decode; any string, since rejected encodings are under test.

jwk_thumbprint_input.description: A JWK (RFC 7517 §4) as a JSON object, imported and then hashed (RFC 7638 §3). Its members are deliberately unconstrained: invalid keys are under test.

jwk_thumbprint_ok.description: The base64url JWK Thumbprint (RFC 7638 §3) and its JWK Thumbprint URI (RFC 9278 §3).

jws_signer.description: One signature to compute: its JWS Protected Header as exact octets (RFC 7515 §5.1 step 3; the runner signs over them verbatim), its JWS Unprotected Header (RFC 7515 §7.2.1), and its key. The runner imports key, then parses protected_b64u, then header; the first error is the outcome.

protected_b64u.description: BASE64URL(UTF8(JWS Protected Header)), kept verbatim for the signing input (e.g. RFC 7515 A.1's CRLF header).

header.description: The JWS Unprotected Header as a JSON object (JSON serializations only). Unconstrained: header errors are under test.

key.description: The signing JWK (RFC 7517 §4) as a JSON object, imported with the library's JWK import. Unconstrained: an import error is the vector's outcome.

jws_sign_input.description: Sign a payload (RFC 7515 §5.1) in one serialization, with one signer (compact, flattened) or several (general, in order), attached or detached (RFC 7515 Appendix F).

payload_b64u.description: The JWS Payload octets, canonical base64url; the runner decodes them (with b64:false, RFC 7797, the octets themselves are signed).

detached.description: Leave the payload out of the output (RFC 7515 Appendix F).

jws_sign_exact.description: A deterministic signature (HMAC, EdDSA): the exact output. A compact JWS is compared as a string; a JSON JWS is compared as a JSON value, so member order does not matter (RFC 8259 §4) but every octet of every string does.

jws_verify_with.description: The key and allow-list a runner verifies its own randomized output with.

jws_sign_roundtrip.description: A randomized signature (ECDSA): the runner checks that its output has the requested serialization's shape, verifies it with verify_with (passing the payload separately when detached), and checks the verified payload equals payload_b64u. Any failure there fails the vector.

jws_verify_input.description: Verify a JWS (RFC 7515 §5.2) with one key and an allow-list (RFC 8725 §3.1), under the processing order of ADR 0026 §2. The runner imports key, then builds the options, then verifies; the first error is the outcome.

key.description: A JWK (RFC 7517 §4) as a JSON object, imported with the library's JWK import. Unconstrained: an import error is the vector's outcome.

detached_payload_b64u.description: The detached payload (RFC 7515 Appendix F); the JWS then carries none.

max_input_len.description: The largest serialized JWS accepted, in octets (ADR 0026 §7); the library default when absent.

max_signatures.description: The most signatures a general JSON JWS may have (ADR 0026 §7); the library default when absent.

jws_verify_ok.description: The verified JWS: its payload, the alg of the signature that verified, and that signature's index (0 for compact and flattened; the first that verifies, in array order, for general, ADR 0026 §3).

keys_import_pem_input.description: Import one RFC 7468 PEM block with the library's PEM key import (ADR 0018 §3): the label selects the structure (PRIVATE KEY: PKCS#8, RFC 5958 §2; PUBLIC KEY: SPKI, RFC 5280 §4.1.2.7; EC PRIVATE KEY: SEC1, RFC 5915 §3; RSA PUBLIC KEY: PKCS#1, RFC 8017 App. A.1.1). Any string, since rejected encodings are under test.

keys_import_pem_ok.description: The imported key as a JWK (RFC 7517 §4), compared as a JSON value: member order is ignored (RFC 8259 §4), every string must match exactly. An imported key never has kty oct and carries no alg.

keys_export_pem_input.description: Export a JWK as one RFC 7468 PEM block in format (ADR 0018 §3). The runner imports jwk with the library's JWK import first; an import error is the vector's outcome.

format.description: pkcs8 (RFC 5958 §2), sec1 (RFC 5915 §3), spki (RFC 5280 §4.1.2.7) or pkcs1 (RFC 8017 App. A.1.1, RSA public keys).

keys_export_pem_ok.description: The exact PEM text: 64-character lines, LF line endings and a final newline, in OpenSSL 4's DER layout (ADR 0018 §3); compared as a string.

keys_import_der_input.description: Import DER in the structure format names, with the library's DER key import (ADR 0018 §3); there is no format sniffing (ADR 0007), and DER of another structure fails. The runner decodes der_b64u (canonical base64url); a value that does not decode canonically is a broken vector, never an outcome.

format.description: pkcs8 (RFC 5958 §2), sec1 (RFC 5915 §3), spki (RFC 5280 §4.1.2.7) or pkcs1 (RFC 8017 App. A.1.1, RSA public keys).

keys_import_der_ok.description: The imported key as a JWK (RFC 7517 §4), compared as a JSON value: member order is ignored (RFC 8259 §4), every string must match exactly. An imported key never has kty oct and carries no alg.

keys_export_der_input.description: Export a JWK as DER in format (ADR 0018 §3), with the format matrix of keys.export_pem. The runner imports jwk with the library's JWK import first; an import error is the vector's outcome.

format.description: pkcs8 (RFC 5958 §2), sec1 (RFC 5915 §3), spki (RFC 5280 §4.1.2.7) or pkcs1 (RFC 8017 App. A.1.1, RSA public keys).

keys_export_der_ok.description: The exact DER, in OpenSSL 4's layout (ADR 0018 §3), as canonical base64url; compared as a string.

keys_generate_for_input.description: Generate a private key for an algorithm with the library's generate_for (ADR 0018 §5) from the OS CSPRNG. alg is a JWS alg, a JWE alg or a JWE enc name, resolved in the one registry of RFC 7518 §7.1 (names unique and case-sensitive); any string, since unknown names are under test.

keys_generated_shape.description: What a generated key is, without its random material: kty, crv (EC and OKP only), the alg the key is bound to (RFC 7517 §4.4) and the length of k in octets (oct only). Compared as a JSON value, so a member the generated key has and the shape omits fails too.

keys_generate_for_ok.description: Generated keys are random, so only their shape is expected. The runner also checks that the key is private, has exactly the members RFC 7518 §6.2.1-§6.2.2 (EC), RFC 8037 §2 (OKP) or RFC 7518 §6.4.1 (oct) define plus alg, and imports back unchanged; any failure there fails the vector.
